articles.title: ¿Tenías contrato con Nextel en estos años? AT&T te dará reembolso
articles.standfirst: Una sentencia judicial obliga a AT&T a devolver pagos realizados por usuarios de Nextel
articles.summary: Una sentencia judicial obliga a AT&T a devolver pagos realizados por usuarios de Nextel
articles.body: Un contrato telefónico firmado hace más de una década podría representar hoy una oportunidad para recuperar dinero. AT&T México informó que existe una sentencia judicial que ordena reembolsar los pagos realizados por antiguos clientes de Nextel, específicamente quienes contrataron el servicio de radio o trunking entre septiembre de 2008 y el 29 de febrero de 2012, debido a deficiencias en su prestación. La resolución contempla no solamente la devolución de las cantidades pagadas, sino también una bonificación adicional del 20%, además de los gastos y honorarios derivados del procedimiento correspondiente. A través de un aviso difundido en sus canales oficiales, la compañía explicó que los usuarios interesados deberán adherirse a la acción colectiva 271/2022, para lo cual disponen de un plazo de 18 meses. La sentencia está dirigida a personas que contrataron el servicio de radio o trunking de Nextel, empresa que posteriormente pasó a formar parte de AT&T México. No se trata de una devolución general para todos los antiguos clientes, sino de una medida relacionada con un servicio específico y un periodo determinado. Los principales requisitos señalados en el aviso son: La cantidad que podría recibir cada persona dependerá de los pagos correspondientes al servicio contratado. La sentencia establece que AT&T debe reembolsar los pagos efectuados por el servicio de radio o trunking, debido a que este no fue prestado de manera eficiente. Además, contempla una bonificación equivalente al 20% de las cantidades correspondientes, junto con los gastos y honorarios que genere el procedimiento. Por ejemplo, si los pagos sujetos a devolución sumaran 5,000 pesos, la bonificación representaría otros 1,000 pesos, para un total ilustrativo de 6,000 pesos, sin considerar otros conceptos. Esta cifra es únicamente un ejemplo matemático y no constituye un monto garantizado para todos los usuarios. Los antiguos clientes interesados pueden acudir al Juzgado Segundo de Distrito en Materia Civil en la Ciudad de México y solicitar información sobre la acción colectiva 271/2022. Otra alternativa es comunicarse con LM Krasovsky Asociados, Sociedad Civil, representante común de la colectividad, a través de Luis Miguel Krasovsky Prieto. Sus datos de contacto están disponibles en El aviso señala que existe un plazo de 18 meses para adherirse, aunque no precisa en el texto difundido la fecha exacta de vencimiento. Para quienes conservaron contratos y comprobantes de pago de Nextel, esta resolución abre la posibilidad de reclamar cantidades correspondientes a un servicio contratado hace más de una década.

articles.title: Herencia: ¿Quién se queda con los bienes si no hay testamento y cuál es el orden de prioridad en México?
articles.standfirst: Esto es lo que pasa cuando una persona muere sin dejar testamento.
articles.summary: Esto es lo que pasa cuando una persona muere sin dejar testamento.
articles.body: El testamento es un documento vital para asegurar el bienestar patrimonial de las familias mexicanas cuando uno de sus integrantes fallece, por lo que es necesario realizar este trámite ante una notaría pública en vida, debido a que en caso de que una persona muera sin este documento, surgen problemas. Y es que muchas veces las familias no se ponen de acuerdo en cuanto a la repartición de los bienes que deja una persona fallecida, aunque el marco legal en México establece claramente el orden de prioridad que tienen los familiares al momento de heredar en este tipo de casos. Cabe señalar que para realizar el testamento en México es necesario: A continuación en MARCA MX te contamos más sobre lo que sucede cuando una persona muere sin dejar testamento. De acuerdo con el marco legal vigente en México, cuando una persona muere sin dejar testamento, aquellas personas que tienen derecho a heredar sus bienes son los descendientes; después la pareja, ya sea en matrimonio o concubinato; los padres y por último otros familiares. También pueden heredar los hermanos de la persona fallecida en caso de que no haya hijos, pareja y padres. Sin embargo este trámite no es automático, ya que es necesario que los interesados inicien un juicio de sucesión intestamentaria para demostrar el derecho que tienen para acceder a esta herencia. En este proceso se convoca a los familiares en el orden antes mencionado para definir qué pasará. Posteriormente se designa un albacea sobre la herencia, para después realizar un inventario y avalúo de los bienes, y se realiza un proyecto de repartición para llegar a un acuerdo y resolución. Por último, se adjudica la herencia a los beneficiarios correspondientes. En caso de que una persona fallezca y no haya familiares para reclamar la herencia, el Estado podrá disponer de los bienes para la beneficencia pública.

Chiefs Kingdom's confidence level hasn't dipped below 89% since the team whooped up on the Denver Broncos in Week 1. There was a one-point percentage drop in confidence frmo Week 5 to Week 6, however.

articles.title: Badgers bounce back from loss to Nebraska with sweep
articles.summary: The Badgers got a sweep in their return to the Field House.
articles.body:
Coming off their loss to the No. 1 Nebraska Cornhuskers, the No. 6 Wisconsin Badgers took care of business at home, beating the Maryland Terrapins 25-18, 25-23, 25-18 in a sweep of their own.

Wisconsin fought hard in the Nebraska loss, and head coach Kelly Sheffield was pleased with his team's performance afterwards. Even with the loss, the Badgers moved back up to No. 6 in the AVCA Top 25, as Florida fell two spots to No. 7.

Wisconsin opened the first set on a 6-1 run, quickly setting the tone as Lynney Tarnow, Eva Travis, and Decelise Champion all got kills. From there, the Badgers never really got into trouble in the first set, and a kill from Champion got them the finish at 25-18.

It was a clean set from Wisconsin, which had 15 kills and only three attack errors, as they hit .500 in the opening frame.

The second set was the closest of the three, as it was Maryland that got out to an early 7-5 lead. But the Badgers went on another 6-1 run, thanks to a pair of kills from Champion, a kill from Travis, and a trio of attack errors on Maryland.

From there, the set was back-and-forth, with the Terrapins even taking a 21-18 lead late on the verge of tying things up at one a piece. But the Badgers rallied to rattle off six straight points before closing the set 25-23 after Maryland brought things to within one. This time, it was a Charlie Fuerbringer kill to seal the deal and put Wisconsin up 2-0.

The third set was close in the early going, with both sides tied at 5. But the Badgers went on a 5-1 run, creating some distance, and they were in control the rest of the set, even when the Terrapins provided some resistance. Wisconsin went on an 8-2 run to go up 18-10, and the Terrapins never got within six, as the Badgers got the sweep with a 25-18 win in the third set.

Wisconsin out-hit Maryland .344 to .155, and Decelise Champion finished with 17 kills and five blocks. Lynney Tarnow also had eight blocks, while Charlie Fuerbringer had 35 assists. Anna Bardaro added 15 digs as well, as she and Kristen Simon both played well.

The Badgers will take on the Iowa Hawkeyes next on Sunday, with first serve set for 1:00 p.m. on Big Ten Network.

SAN FRANCISCO — The "defense wins championships" crowd will have a new case study to evaluate after the best-of-seven WNBA Finals series between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream wraps.

The Valkyries had the best defensive rating during the regular season, while the Dream were third. The Dream led the league in steals per game, while the Valkyries were fourth. The series, as a result, will come down to which team can maintain composure and win the possession battle. In Game 1 on Saturday afternoon, the Valkyries answered the bell with a 68-64 win against the fourth-seeded Dream.

Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 26 points, while Allisha Gray returned from a hand injury to lead the Dream with 19 points.

The Dream will try to even the series Monday at the Chase Center.

articles.title: Army football's Cale Hellums drawing comparisons to Bryson Daily
articles.summary: Army football's Cale Hellums drawing comparisons to Bryson Daily after 5-TD game vs FAU.
articles.body:
Check out our Army football vs FAU photo gallery, best images

Samari Howard received a sideline apology.

Cale Hellums was in a giving mood following Saturday's 56-24 rout of Florida Atlantic , and why not? Army's senior quarterback has a lot of good fortune to spread around.

The parallels between Hellums and Daily are becoming more clear every week. Daily took over as starter as a junior in 2023 and blossomed during a 12-2 senior campaign in 2024, posting a nation-high 32 rushing touchdowns and finishing sixth in Heisman Trophy voting.

Hellums learned much under Daily and became his heir apparent in 2025. Running the same offense and showing the same drive and spirit, Hellums guided Army to a Fenway Bowl victory, and now has the Black Knights (4-2) just two wins from another bowl berth.

And now Hellums and Daily share a line in the Army record books. Hellums rushed for five touchdowns against Florida Atlantic , tying the Academy record set by Daily nearly two years earlier to the day in a five-TD effort against East Carolina in 2024.

"Bryson's a great friend of mine,'' Hellums said. "He was an awesome teammate and someone that I looked up to when I was playing behind him.''

Hellums great in red zone for Army football

Hellums said he had no idea at the time that he had tied Daily's mark with an extra-effort 1-yard score early in the fourth quarter against FAU – he did know he already had four because when he followed fullback Jake Rendina into the end zone from 3 yards out late in the third. He paused in the end zone and counted out 1, 2, 3, 4 on his hand to celebrate.

Of the record-tying tally, "To be able to match that is pretty cool,'' Hellums said. "Definitely the competitor in me wanted to beat it, but I'll send (Daily) a funny text.''

What's also funny and heart-warming was his sideline reaction following the fourth score. On the play previous, split back Samari Howard went into motion, received the short "flip'' pass off the snap and got a hard 2 yards when he needed three. Hellums tried to go over the top on the next play, rolled left off his line and a defender and reached back, stretching the ball over the goal line. It was initially ruled a stop by the officials, but a video review showed Hellums had gotten the score.

In a conversation heard on the sidelines, Hellums apologized to Samari over getting the score (not to worry, because Howard produced the game's first touchdown on a 30-yard pitch play from Hellums just 21 seconds in).

For the most part, Hellums tries to remain even-keeled on the field, but he showed off a "lean at the tape' – much like a sprinter at the finish line – as he completed a 58-yard burst off the left side early in the first quarter, matching a score of equal career-best length a week earlier against Tulane.

This season, Hellums has 13 rushing touchdowns and 719 yards on 129 carries; last season, he had 18 rushing scores, and 1,223 yards on 304 carries. For his career (which includes a few appearances in relief in 2024), Hellums has 31 rushing scores and 1,970 yards on 450 carries.

Hellums had two rushing scores in the opener against Bryant, three in the win at Temple and two against Tulane. Hellums' 25-carry effort against FAU (netting 195 yards) comes a week after posting 38 carries and a career-high 223 yards vs. Tulane, the 11th-best rushing effort in Army history.

"He's certainly playing much better this year than he did a year ago,'' praised Army head coach Jeff Monken. "And, much like Bryson Daily during his junior year, has some games where it was really a struggle and didn't play as well as he would have liked. His senior year (Daily) played much better. ... It comes with experience and comes with the confidence of getting that experience.

"He (Hellums) also knows that he's our quarterback, which is kind of where he was a year ago, even at this point. So I think just that growth and maturity and he's just playing well, taking care of the ball - that's the most important thing that he's done.''

articles.title: Texas football: Steve Sarkisian doesn't rule out benching Arch Manning after Florida loss
articles.summary: At the beginning of this season, Arch Manning was considered among the top quarterbacks in the country. But the Texas football team's 27-24 loss at home to F...
articles.body:
At the beginning of this season, Arch Manning was considered a Heisman Trophy front-runner and one of the top quarterbacks in the country. But after the second-year starter again struggled in Texas football's 27-24 loss at home to unranked Florida on Saturday, is it time for a change?

Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian wouldn't rule it out after the game. After the stunning setback , Sarkisian was asked if he had thought about making a change at quarterback. Sarkisian answered, "I just felt like we didn't play good offensive football and we're not playing great offensive football right now. So everything is going to be evaluated."

Does the evaluation of everything include Manning's job status?

"Everything means everything," Sarkisian bluntly stated.

Sarkisian was later again asked about Manning's performance. He said there was plenty of blame to go around for Saturday's loss. As a team, Texas collected 272 yards and had just four drives go longer than five plays. In the third quarter, UT gained eight yards while running four plays.

"It'd be easy for me to say, 'Hey, Arch was the problem today.' Was Arch perfect? No, but nobody was perfect on offense today," Sarkisian said. "We took turns today, and that's where I have to look at every aspect of what we're doing because if it was one person, it'd be easy. Yeah, change one guy and everything's going to be great. Well, I don't think that that was all the issue today. Could he have been better? No doubt about it. But there's some other issues that need to be addressed."

Texas, No. 7 in the Associated Press poll, will surely slip when the new rankings are released Sunday. Texas (4-2, 1-2) will attempt to snap its two-game losing streak next week at home against Ole Miss.

Arch Manning, Texas offense have surprising struggles against Florida

Against a Florida secondary that ranked last in the SEC (and 131st among 138 FBS-level teams) in passing yardage by allowing 268.7 yards per game, Manning threw for just 173 yards and a touchdown while completing 14 of his 20 passes. A 62-yard connection with Emmett Mosley V while Texas was trailing by 10 points in the fourth quarter accounted for around 35% of Manning's yardage total.

Manning didn't throw an interception, but he did lose a costly fumble while taking a sack on UT's final drive and he was dropped for a loss on another fourth-down attempt in the fourth quarter. Last week, Manning threw two interceptions in the fourth quarter that led to 10 points in a 27-24 loss to Oklahoma .

"We talk about winning the fourth quarter, and we didn't do that today," Manning said. "Moving forward, we've got to win the fourth."

When told afterward about Sarkisian's evaluation comment, Manning said "everyone's evaluated every week. That's how it is at a school like this. Elite players, so everyone's got to get better, and it starts with me."

Through six games, Manning has thrown for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions while completing 63.9% of his passes. He's leading an offense that has yet to score more than 24 points against a Power Four defense.

Texas has not wholly benched its starting quarterback for a non-injury reason since Sarkisian's first season in 2021 when Casey Thompson replaced Hudson Card after a disastrous September defeat at Arkansas. Behind Manning on the Texas depth chart are sophomore KJ Lacey and freshman Dia Bell . Both were highly-rated recruits, but Lacey has thrown only nine passes in his college career while Bell has yet to get into a game at Texas.

articles.summary: “I'm probably harder on myself than anybody and I'll evaluate this game the same way."
articles.body:
AUSTIN — After a stunning 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators in which the No. 7 Texas Longhorns only ran 19 plays for 96 yards in the second half — 62 0f which came on a desperation heave on 4th and 7 down 10 points with five minutes left in the game — head coach Steve Sarkisian said that he's going to have a long night.

The Longhorns had already had a long day.

Did he think of making a change away from struggling senior quarterback Arch Manning, who missed too many open receivers, took too many sacks, and committed another game-changing turnover when he fumbled on a sack with two minutes remaining and the Longhorns down three points?

"I just felt like we didn't we play good offensive football and we're not playing great offensive football right now, so everything is going to be evaluated," Sarkisian said.

What happened to the offense after scoring 10 points on the first two drives?

"Failure to to do our job well, not calling good enough plays, not winning one on ones," Sarkisian said. "I mean, it's all of it. That's my point. It's like, I have to evaluate everything."

What were Sarkisian's impressions of how Manning played? When he says everything is evaluated, does that include…

"Everything means everything," Sarkisian interrupted.

How do does Sarkisian balance changing personnel versus improving the personnel the Longhorns are already using?

"That's part of the evaluation. We need to figure that out," Sarkisian said.

After all the effort put into this season, why are things not clicking and heading in this direction?

"No, that's the frustrating part, and the frustrating part is we practice really well," Sarkisian said. "We're in a great frame of mind to go execute, and we're not, and so that's part of the evaluation. I've got to look at it all to figure out where is the disconnect."

"I think details and route running, I think pass protection, picking up blitzes, I think not being able to run the ball for two yards in short yardage, just to name a few that pop into my head," Sarkisian said.

What changes has Sarkisian made to his play calling or has he stuck to his base offense over the last three games? Does he anticipate making…

"We're going to evaluate everything," Sarkisain said, interrupting another reporter. "I don't know how many times I need to say we're going to evaluate everything from an offensive perspective. Part of that is play call."

What process will Sarkisian use to evaluate himself as a play caller?

"The process is the same process that I use every weekend. I evaluate everything that we do, from the game plan itself to the play calls themselves to who was touching the ball to how did we block to what do we call in specific situations to how did every individual perform, myself included," Sarkisian said.

"I don't take it personally evaluating myself — I'm probably harder on myself than anybody and I'll evaluate this game the same way. I'm sure there's going to be situations I'm going to be really hard on myself because we weren't good enough."

Sarkisian speaks frequently about not concerning himself with what people outside the football facility think, but if he wants to challenge the assertion that he's harder on himself than anybody else, taking a look at social media might give him a different perspective on that.

articles.title: Florida football coach Jon Sumrall trolls Texas after Gators upset Longhorns
articles.summary: Florida head coach Jon Sumrall trolled Texas after Saturday's win.
articles.body:
Florida pulled off a massive upset over No. 7 Texas in Austin on Saturday.

The Gators walked into Austin and beat the Longhorns 27-24, improving to 5-2 overall. Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning struggled again, throwing for 173 yards and one touchdown, while not seeing the field very well.

He also fumbled at the end of the fourth quarter, giving the Gators the ball back, and they never gave it back to the Longhorns.

After the game, Gators head coach Jon Sumrall trolled the Longhorns by wearing a cowboy hat as he was walking out of the stadium.

A massive win for Jon Sumrall and the Gators

Sep 19, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall watches his team warm up before the game against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Saturday's win snapped a two-game losing streak for the Gators after they started the season with a perfect 4-0 record. They now have serious momentum going into their next game against the Georgia Bulldogs on Halloween.

Gators quarterback Tramell Jones finished the game with 155 yards through the air and two touchdowns, while also rushing for 41 yards. It was the first start of his career since Aaron Philo is dealing with an injury.

Considering how well Jones played on Saturday, he may be in line for another start against the Bulldogs, even if Philo is ready to return.

articles.title: No. 1 Ferris State football overcomes early deficit to beat No. 1 GVSU
articles.summary: Another epic Anchor Bone Classic is in the books. It lived up to the hype.
articles.body:
ALLENDALE - Top-ranked Ferris State trailed early but quickly turned things around against No. 13 Grand Valley State.

The Bulldogs snagged an interception and a fumble in the second quarter to erase a 17-point deficit and propel them to a 41-34 win over the Lakers in the Anchor Bone Classic on Saturday, Oct. 17, at Lubbers Stadium in Allendale.

Wyatt Bower scored on a 3-yard run early in the second quarter. Zak Ahearn scored on a 10-yard run before Jay Cady kicked a 25-yard field goal. FSU put in its other kicker, Eoin O'Sullivan, who nailed a 46-yard field goal putting the Bulldogs up 20-17 at halftime.

Bower started the third quarter with a 16-yard touchdown run, then threw a 32-yard scoring strike to Tae Boyd to make it 34-17.

The Lakers, who held a 17-0 early lead, didn't score again until 54 seconds remaining in the third quarter when Andrew Schuster threw his third touchdown pass of the game, a 61-yard strike to Kellen Reed.

But a field goal and a Schuster TD pass to Kellen Russell-Dixon pulled the Lakers within 41-34 with 4:17 to go.

This is a developing story and will be updated with details and reaction.

articles.title: WATCH: Texas A&M HC provides update on junior wide receiver
articles.summary: Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko said the Aggies are supporting and praying for Ashton Bethel-Roman, amid his absence for personal matters.
articles.body:
It wasn't all good news for Texas A&M football after a 41-0 shutout win on Saturday , as head coach Mike Elko provided an update on the Aggies ' talented junior wide receiver.

Ashton Bethel-Roman did not attend Saturday's home contest against The Citadel due to personal reasons and is being "given space" by the team to deal with the matter. This comes after Bethel-Roman dealt with an injury earlier in the year, before making a return back to the lineup recently.

He was named the starter at the beginning of the season, but has caught just seven passes for 56 yards in five games played through the first seven weeks. Bethel Roman has been targeted 15 times in 2026, which is fourth among the wide receiving corps, behind Isaiah Horton, Mario Craver and Aaron Gregory.

Here's Elko's update on Bethel-Roman in the postgame press conference via TexAgs :

Texas A&M's wideout group keeps getting lighter each week. Terry Bussey and Madden Williams are out for the year and Mario Craver, Marcel Reed's top target, has also seen limited action over recent weeks while dealing with an injury. Fortunately, rising stars like Gregory and TK Norman stepped up for the Aggies in their Week 7 shutout of The Citadel, hauling in 11 combined receptions for 182 yards and two touchdowns.

Bethel-Roman being out of the rotation is a massive hit for Elko and company. With multiple huge SEC contests rapidly approaching, the health and overall status of Texas A&M's offense, especially the wide receiving corps, could be detrimental moving forward.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois destroys Fabio Wardley in blistering fashion to fulfil rematch vow
articles.summary: Wardley’s trainer Ben Davison threw in the towel, five months on from being criticised for not pulling his man out against Dubois in the first match
articles.body:
Daniel Dubois left no doubt in the mind as he knocked out Fabio Wardley inside two rounds, fulfilling his vow to make quick work of his British heavyweight rival in their rematch.

Having been the one to succumb to an early knockdown in the first matchup, Dubois came out of the blocks in blistering fashion and sent Wardley to the canvas inside 17 seconds.

Wardley, weathering a first-round firestorm, attempted to respond with a huge right cross of his own up against the ropes which narrowly missed.

But Dubois continued to pummel his rival and threatened to put him away as the round came to a close, Wardley's trainer Ben Davison holding the towel seemingly ready to pull his man out before the Ipswich man was saved by the bell.

The punishment continued as the second round began, rocking Wardley with a sharp one-two before he was forced into a corner once again, with Dubois's attacks overwhelming his British rival.

This time Davison did throw in the towel, something he was criticised for not doing in the first fight , to seal Wardley's fate and ensure Dubois retained his world title.

"Shout out to everybody, shoutout to my dad, my whole team. Fabio is a great warrior, but it was my time, my era," Dubois said.

"I had bad intentions from the beginning. Our back was against the wall first time. We just had to go out there and show we meant business tonight."

Wardley is now left to bounce back from two consecutive losses having entered the year undefeated.

He said: "It's never fun to lose. It is what it is, I've always thrown myself in with the biggest, toughest, meanest guys around, there's no shame in testing yourself against the best.

"Daniel is testament to coming again and I'll come again. You come with a game plan, try to adjust things and it didn't work tonight. It's credit to Daniel of how well he prepared."

Wardley came into the mammoth heavyweight rematch off the back of a brutal defeat in the British pair's first meeting back in May, when he failed to take advantage of two early knockdowns before Dubois showed immense heart, turning the tide and eventually stopping Wardley in the 11th round.

The 31-year-old Ipswich man was left battered and bloodied by the time the referee eventually waved off the clash at Manchester's Co-op Live, his nose smashed in and right eye near-completely shut. There was criticism of his corner, chiefly trainer Ben Davison, for not throwing in the towel earlier.

Wardley, however, told promoter Frank Warren of his desire to rematch Dubois immediately following the first bout , revealing this request was made in his dressing room before leaving the arena.

Wardley was insistent that he was in a better position to make adjustments from the first bout compared to Dubois, saying that the room for growth was "exponentially in my favour", despite being the older man by two years.

Dubois was the heavier man on the night by a slender margin of five pounds, though both fighters took to the scale at career-heaviest weights at Friday's ceremonial weigh-in in London's Old Spitalfields Market.

And despite Wardley's confidence, Dubois put on an emphatic display to finish his British rival in short order, taking a step towards his goal of becoming undisputed champion at heavyweight.

Dubois has already fought and failed in the pursuit of undisputed gold, knocked out by Oleksandr Usyk under the Wembley arch in July 2025, his previous fight before facing Wardley earlier this year.

He is now looks set to target another heavyweight champion after Usyk vacated his titles earlier this year, and squared off with IBF holder Filip Hrgovic - who stunted British 21-year-old Moses Itauma's stunning rise in August - in the ring after his second triumph over Wardley.

articles.title: Dutch Darts Championship: Michael van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Gian van Veen makes history and Gerwyn Price triumphs on return
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen's poor form in 2026 continues as he suffers second-round Dutch Darts Championship defeat to Williams O'Connor; Gerwyn Price, Gian van Veen, Stephen Bunting, Nathan Aspinall each progress; watch Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
The defeat extends Van Gerwen's poor run of form, having lost his opening match at four European Tour events this season before arriving in Maastricht: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It marks his most first-round exits in a single season since the tour began in 2012.

O'Connor produced a superb display, firing in three ton-plus checkouts of 136, 131 and 121 to seal his victory and book his place in round three.

Elsewhere on Saturday, Gerwyn Price's return to the stage ended in glory as he beat Scott Williams 6-3, while Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average.

Martin Schindler and Stephen Bunting also jumped into the qualification spots for Dortmund.

Van Veen averaged a staggering 120.24 in whitewashing Sebastian Bialecki, breaking the previous record of 118.66 by Dave Chisnall.

Schindler sealed his spot at the European Championships later this month with his victory over Karel Sedlacek.

Bunting left it late to secure his place at the European Championship, beating already-qualified Cameron Menzies 6-2 to book his spot. The former Masters champion needed a strong finish to get over the line.

The 41-year-old pinned six out of ten attempts at the outer ring in his victory over the Scot, and jumped into the qualifying places, knocking Kim Huybrechts out of the running.

Brendan Dolan remains the only player capable of pushing Sedlacek out of the European Championship qualifying spots after beating Heine Uuldriks 6-4. The Northern Irishman had led 4-1 before being pegged back.

Nathan Aspinall ended Michael Smith's hopes of qualifying for Dortmund with a dominant 6-1 victory. The World Grand Prix semi-finalist averaged over 102 to dispatch the former world champion.

Wessel Nijman and Danny Noppert also secured their places in Sunday's action, with the Dutch pair defeating Jeffrey De Graaf and Dave Chisnall respectively.

Niels Zonneveld edged a last-leg decider against Krzysztof Ratajski, hitting seven maximums for the second consecutive match to book his place in round three. Fellow Dutchman Jermaine Wattimena also progressed, beating Host Nation Qualifier Jimmy van Schie 6-2.

European Tour ranking leader Ross Smith will face Ryan Searle in round three after overcoming Ryan Joyce and Dirk van Duijvenbode respectively.

Damon Heta averaged over 103 in a dominant 6-1 victory over Jonny Clayton, securing his first win against the Welshman since May last year.

Luke Woodhouse also booked his place in Sunday's action with a comfortable victory over Andrew Gilding.

Cristo Reyes brought the evening's action to a close in style, averaging over 110 in a 6-2 win against Chris Dobey while converting 60 per cent of his attempts at double.

The Dutch Darts Championship concludes with a bumper double session on Sunday, as the final 16 players battle it out for the title in Maastricht.

articles.title: Unranked Auburn upsets top-ranked Georgia with walk-off field goal, marking wild feat not seen in 36 years
articles.summary: Kirby Smart's Bulldogs blew a 14-0 lead at home as Auburn's Alex McPherson drilled a 34-yard field goal to seal the shocking 27-24 upset win.
articles.body: Being ranked No. 1 in the country might actually be a curse. For the first time since 1990, the No. 1 team in the nation lost to an unranked opponent in consecutive weeks after Georgia fell at home to Auburn, 27-24. Georgia had defeated 53 consecutive unranked opponents. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE It looked like all Georgia early, as they got out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. But the Dogs would not score on their next five drives, punting three times, missing a field goal and throwing a pick. The Tigers used that all to their advantage and scored 24 unanswered points to put Georgia on upset alert. The Bulldogs entered the fourth quarter down 10, but an early field goal cut the deficit, and they were able to force two Auburn punts. After the second, they embarked on a 13-play, 94-yard touchdown drive to tie the game. Auburn was stuffed and had to punt the ball away for a third consecutive drive, giving Georgia the ball at its own 39 with over a minute to go and all the momentum. They got a gift with a defensive pass interference on the first play. But suddenly, all that momentum shifted. On the next play, Gunnar Stockton lost a fumble, giving Auburn and all three of its timeouts the ball with 58 seconds at its own 44. OHIO STATE SNAPS INDIANA'S 22-GAME WINNING STREAK, HANDS REIGNING CHAMPS FIRST LOSS SINCE 2024 IN THRILLER The Tigers got 22 yards on three straight carries and then drew a roughing the passer penalty, putting themselves in chip-shot range. Alex McPherson came on for a 34-yard field goal, and he drilled it to complete the upset. Texas lost the Red River Rivalry to Oklahoma last week, causing it to drop all the way to No. 7, in case you are wondering how far Georgia may fall. This is also Georgia's first unranked opponent loss at home under Kirby Smart since 2019. Georgia, now 5-1, had taken the top spot after it defeated Alabama last week in a dogfight, but the spot is now up for grabs for squads like No. 2 Notre Dame, No. 3 Miami and No. 4 Ohio State. Auburn, meanwhile, will host No. 22 LSU next week.

articles.title: Indiana’s first loss in almost 2 years shows Hoosiers a new, painful side to being in college football’s top tier
articles.summary: Descending the stairwell back to Earth — after a delirious 22-game win streak came screeching to a stunning end, after the biggest football game in a generation on the Indiana campus fizzled to a disastrous 19-15 loss to Ohio State on a boneheaded play more reminiscent of the pre-delirium era — Indiana football officially arrived.
articles.body: Descending the stairwell back to Earth — after a delirious 22-game win streak came screeching to a stunning end, after the biggest football game in a generation on the Indiana campus fizzled to a disastrous 19-15 loss to Ohio State on a boneheaded play more reminiscent of the pre-delirium era — Indiana football officially arrived. Fans who opted to walk down from the top of Memorial Stadium rather than take the elevator took turns venting their frustration about the loss, their ire growing as if they were descending through Dante’s levels of Hell. The first circle belonged to Nick Marsh, who — if you’re being kind — mistimed his fancy footwork (or, if you were in the stairwell, wildly fouled up). On fourth-and-four — fourth-and-ballgame, fourth-and-win streak, fourth-and-dethroning Big Ten royalty Ohio State — Marsh snuck to the left edge of the end zone. He was so wide open that, when TV cameras showed the replay, there was literally no one else - not an Indiana player, not an Ohio State defender - in the shot. The Hoosiers paid handsomely for their big pickup via the transfer portal, luring him from Michigan State. Marsh easily hauled in the pass from Josh Hoover and took a step into the end zone. Or at least that was the idea. On Marsh’s first step, he casually put down his left foot and the outside edge of his cleat caught the white edge that rims the red paint marking out of bounds. As in-game operators mistakenly shot off fireworks, Marsh put his hands on his head, immediately aware of his mistake. No touchdown. No win. No win streak. No unseating the kings. “Butt naked f**king wide open,’’ one fan screamed as he marched down the stairs. Another bemoaned the amount of money spent on Marsh’s NIL deal, using similar obscene language. Spiraling downward, next came Josh Howard’s undressing. The TCU transfer quarterback completed 20 of 40 passes, regularly sailing passes over even the super-glue-sure hands of Charlie Becker. He wasn’t awful, but he wasn’t great, committing the cardinal sin of being human. That is not a familiar affliction here, not after the practically sainted Fernando Mendoza taught people about fiscal responsibility, hobnobbed with priests at the local Catholic church, charmed mothers and zinged passes on Saturdays like a video game avatar. “It wouldn’t have come to this,’’ a woman screamed over her shoulder to a trailing pack of similarly combustible Hoosiers, “if we didn’t f**k around.’’ And finally, as the stairway gave way to the ground, there came the final hard smack of reality. Thousands of people, accustomed to leaving their gridiron grounds in glee, were rendered near speechless as they morosely walked out the gates. One man, summing up the shock, anger and frustration for everyone, stared straight ahead and at one in particular, gathering up whatever air was left in his lungs and yelled one more f-bomb for good measure. Indiana becomes a football school Welcome to success, Indiana. Isn’t it awful? It begets the most precious and precarious gift of all in sports - the joy and misery of expectation. In the grand scheme of things, in the 2026 football season that remains very much viable for the Hoosiers, this loss is barely a flesh wound. But forgive Indiana fans their level of reaction. They have not tasted this particular pleasant poison before. For the past two-plus seasons, happy Hoosier fans have lived in a near-fugue state, their historically impossibly awful team becoming the best in the land. Until this glorious fall Saturday afternoon gave way to the hints of early evening, Indiana football — once the losingest team in all of college football — hadn’t tasted their ordinary helping of defeat for 666 days. Counted in that giddy stretch of unexpected euphoria was actual perfection, a run from August through January without defeat, capped off with, of all ridiculous things, a national championship. So new was the entire concept of winning that, for a hot minute, it was fair to question if Indiana really understood its new place in the hierarchy. It still felt quaint, as if IU hadn’t quite embraced the arrogance they suddenly were in ownership of. Fans walked around downtown in gear declaring their dominance - national championship tees and Rose Bowl jackets - and businesses hung signs in homage to their head coach’s brashness. A blackboard outside of Pitaya, a women’s clothing store, cleverly declared, “It’s simple. We’re the cutest. Google us,” referring to Curt Cignetti’s introductory words at his first press conference - though odds are strong that the coach never much worried about his OOTD (outfit of the day). But a bartender’s lament about the overwhelming crowd mid-afternoon at The Tap felt a little, well, misplaced. The place was full, but compared to Oxford, Mississippi a month ago or State College on the eve of a white out, it didn’t quite hit the mayhem stage. There was no line to get in. Even the wait at the popular Nick’s Hut was short up until at least 4 p.m. And while the marquee on the Buskirk-Chumley Theatre declared, “Buckle Up, Buckeyes. This is Hoosier Country,’’ Ohio State fans walked around town largely unmolested. Try that during, say, “The Game” between Ohio State and Michigan next month, or during the Iron Bowl at either Auburn or Alabama. To be fair, Bloomington eventually got its dog on. People started lining up pre-dawn to find a place in the Breakfast Club, the morning drinking gameday den at The Upstairs Pub, and the tailgating lots were full despite the noon kickoff. It still felt Midwest polite. ‘It sucks, you know?’ Until it wasn’t. Because it was not just the loss but the way IU lost that stung. Under Cignetti, the Hoosiers have been equal parts flawless and gutty, refusing to make mistakes to lose games and always finding ways to win them. They named a popular beer here the 4th and 5 Cream Ale, in reference and deference to Mendoza’s gutty 12-yard touchdown run in the national title game on fourth and five. That was the standard. A week after the defense was gashed by Nebraska, the offense sputtered to find its rhythm. “It sucks, you know?” Becker said. “There were a lot of opportunities, a lot of areas we could have capitalized on. We left a lot short here and that’s frustrating to feel like we kind of beat ourselves in this game.” Trailing 7-3, Indiana drove to the Buckeyes’ 14, but Hoover missed a wide-open Brock Schott on third down. A doinked field goal off the left upright left Indiana with nothing to show for its 66-yard drive. To start the second half, Hoover found Davion Chandler for a quick slant, but Chandler fumbled, the first time the Hoosiers had coughed up the ball in 1,437 plays. Another third-quarter possession ended at Ohio State’s 33, when Hoover was panicked on a blindside blitz and after a miscommunication on third-and-six late in the third, Cignetti had to settle for a 55-yard field goal try. It didn’t work. The most painful, of course, came as it always does - at the end. In what may count as the real biggest news out of this game, Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin left the game after a sack in the fourth quarter. Buckeye coach Ryan Day said he will be out “several weeks,’’ which might cause a legit shakeup not just in the Big Ten, but in the national title race and the Heisman chase (star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith could use his QB to get him the ball). Backup Luke Fahey did his best to not drown as the Buckeyes held the slim 4–point lead, but when Hoover and the Hoosiers started marching down the field with time closing, it felt like another miracle in the making. Indiana has hosted exactly three ranked-on-ranked games since 1993 - entirely because Indiana for so long wasn’t ranked - and one came during the Covid-19 pandemic when 1,034 showed up to watch No. 23 IU versus No. 22 Michigan State. This, No. 5 Indiana versus No. 4 Ohio State, was the big one. Though the Hoosiers bested the Buckeyes in last year’s Big Ten Championship and won the title, Ohio State remains the Big Ten standard. In its entire existence, Indiana beat OSU at home twice, once in 1988 when then the stench of the loss bothered Ohio State coach John Cooper so much that he remarked afterward, “they are either a great football team or we are pathetic,” and once in 1904, when Frank ‘Bunny’ Hare scored on two dropkicks for an 8-0 win, inspiring Indiana students to go wild “parading in the streets clad in their night shirts,” per the Indianapolis Star. And with the win and all of that history right there in his hands, all Marsh had to do was put his foot down. “It’s not Nick’s fault, right?” Hoover said. “Like if I put it a little bit further inside, it’s an easy catch, right?” Hoover said. Smarting and humbled, the players insisted that this will only make them better but they, too, have been spoiled by success. This season has been pockmarked by teams winning big games and falling flat the next; Indiana has to go to Michigan next week to try and buck that trend. “The sun will come up tomorrow,” said Cignetti, whose Little Orphan Annie-esque optimism might have been only slightly less unsettling than the actual loss. “Everything is still ahead of us. We can accomplish everything that we want except going undefeated.” A fair, reasonable summation, even if people here aren’t in the mood right now to be fair or reasonable

articles.title: Ole Miss defense takes charge, shuts down Missouri's high-powered rushing attack in 31-3 win
articles.summary: Ole Miss held Missouri to just 39 rushing yards as Pete Golding's defense completely smothered Austin Simmons and the No. 13 Tigers in a rout.
articles.body: Despite his defensive background, Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding was starting to field some uncomfortable questions about his side of the ball. That tends to happen when you give up 52 points like the Rebels did three weeks ago against Florida. What a difference 21 days makes. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Ole Miss completely smothered one of the best offenses in the SEC en route to a 31-3 drubbing over number 13 Missouri. The Tigers came into today's matchup boasting a top-ten rushing attack and one of the nation's top quarterbacks in Austin Simmons, though you wouldn't have been able to tell after watching this game. Give all the credit to Golding and the Rebels' defense, as the team held Mizzou to 39 yards rushing and harrassed Simmons all game. The senior signal caller looked uncomfortable for virtually the entire game, throwing for 340 yards but needing nearly 50 attempts to do so. LANE KIFFIN CAUGHT LYING ABOUT LSU-OLE MISS SERIES WHILE COMPLAINING ABOUT NINE-GAME SEC SCHEDULE On the other side of the ball, Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss wasn't perfect but came through when the Rebs needed him, tossing three scores and adding another on the ground. It was the Ole Miss rushing attack that really torched the Tigers' run defense. The Rebels racked up 257 yards on the ground in large part because of the efforts of Kewan Lacy and backup Makhi Frazier. Missouri looked as though they were heading for a potential College Football Playoff berth, but a blowout loss against the Rebels changes the calculus of things. Meanwhile, Ole Miss is right back on track with all of their goals still in front of them. The Rebels will go on the road to play a reeling Texas Longhorns team, but things don't get much easier in terms of a path to an SEC Championship and beyond. articles.title: Auburn stuns No. 1 Georgia as college football’s top ranked team loses for second straight week
articles.summary: Alex McPherson kicked a game-winning 34-yard field goal as time expired and Auburn, led by quarterback Byrum Brown’s dominant running game, upset No. 1 Georgia 27-24 on Saturday.
articles.body: Alex McPherson kicked a game-winning 34-yard field goal as time expired and Auburn, led by quarterback Byrum Brown’s dominant running game, upset No. 1 Georgia 27-24 on Saturday. It’s the second straight week the top team in the AP Top 25 lost to an unranked foe after then-No. 1 Texas fell to Oklahoma last Saturday. Auburn’s win meant the team ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 lost in consecutive weeks for the first time since October 1990, according to ESPN. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton led a long game-tying touchdown drive in the fourth quarter but lost a fumble with 58 seconds remaining and the Bulldogs driving for a potential go-ahead field goal. Stockton, who also threw two interceptions, fumbled on a run from the Auburn 46. Safety Sylvester Smith-Reed recovered for the Tigers at the Auburn 44. A roughing-the-passer penalty on Georgia’s Gabe Harris Jr. helped set up McPherson’s game-winning kick. Auburn players swarmed the field. “It’s pretty neat,” said Auburn first-year coach Alex Golesh. “I’m really proud of our guys. Really proud of them. “We’re going to build Auburn back to where everybody wants it, one game at a time. Just hang with us.” Brown ran for 115 yards and a touchdown on 26 carries and added a scoring pass. Georgia (6-1, 4-1 Southeastern Conference) saw its streaks of nine straight wins over Auburn and 53 consecutive wins over unranked teams come to an end in a loss that also will end the Bulldogs’ short one-week stay atop the AP Top 25. Auburn (4-2, 2-2) beat the Bulldogs on the ground, outrushing Georgia 192-113. Tailback Nate Frazier returned from a rib injury to start for Georgia but was ineffective, gaining only 19 yards on nine carries. Georgia trailed 24-14 before rallying with a 42-yard field goal by Peyton Woodring. Stockton led a tying touchdown drive that began at the Georgia 6 and covered 94 yards in 13 plays, capped by his 4-yard pass to London Humphreys. Stockton’s two interceptions doubled his previous season total through six games. The Bulldogs also were hurt by mistakes, including three personal foul penalties. “We helped them,” said Georgia coach Kirby Smart. “We had three turnovers and critical penalties. … We had some really, really untimely, uncharacteristic and undisciplined penalties.” After Georgia took a 14-0 lead, Auburn scored the next 24 points. Georgia looked dominant in the opening minutes, even after Stockton had to leave after hitting the field helmet-first on the first play of the game. Ryan Puglisi completed each of his three passes, including a 41-yarder to Craig Dandridge Jr., before Dwight Phillips’ 15-yard scoring run. Stockton returned for the next possession and threw a 24-yard touchdown pass to tight end Lawson Luckie for the 14-0 lead. Auburn responded with a physical run-first attack led by the 235-pound Brown, who was effective both on designed runs and when taking off after dropping back to pass. Another streak ends Top-ranked teams had won 93 consecutive home games against unranked teams since LSU lost to Arkansas 50-48 in two overtimes on Nov. 23, 2007. Another TD pass for Neptune Auburn’s first touchdown came on a trick play. Brown pitched to wide receiver Christian Neptune who launched a 28-yard touchdown pass to Keshaun Singleton. Georgia defensive backs Ja’Marley Riddle and Ellis Robinson IV collided in the end zone. Riddle was the fill-in starter for KJ Bolden, who wore a walking boot on his right foot and did not play. It was Neptune’s second completion — and second touchdown pass — of the season. Brown completed 15 of 26 passes for 150 yards and one touchdown. Stinger for Stockton Smart said Stockton was cleared after being checked for a concussion following the opening drive but also was seen by trainers following a hit to his throwing shoulder. “He had a stinger in his shoulder that numbs your shoulder,” Smart said. “That happens a lot in football.” Stockton completed 22 of 34 passes for 272 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. The takeaway Auburn: The Tigers, coming off an open week, scored the final 17 points of the first half in an impressive answer to giving up the first 14 points. Brown threw a 9-yard touchdown pass to Chas Nimrod, but his lead role in the Tigers’ running attack was most valuable. Brown wore down the Georgia defense with his physical runs. Jeremiah Cobb also was effective as the running back complement to Brown’s lead role. Georgia: One week after a much-anticipated 20-17 win at No. 6 Alabama, the Bulldogs appeared to fade in the second quarter as its defense was on the field for 45 plays in the first half. The failure to maintain momentum after taking a 14-0 lead on its first two possessions was due to more than fatigue, however. A personal foul on a late hit on Brown by freshman linebacker Khamari Brooks was the big play in Auburn’s tying touchdown drive. Stockton looked at intended receiver Humphreys too long on a pass that was intercepted by Anquon Fegans later in the first half. Up next Auburn plays No. 22 Louisiana State, which beat No. 16 Mississippi State 31-0 on Saturday, at Auburn next Saturday. Georgia has an off week before playing Florida, which upset No. 7 Texas 27-24 on Saturday, on October 31 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.

articles.title: Freshman Tommy Carr's second-half magic leads Michigan to must-have win over Penn State
articles.summary: Tommy Carr replaced Bryce Underwood and scored his first career touchdown as Michigan stunned Penn State in a Big Ten rivalry clash at the Big House.
articles.body: Every season, one of the most anticipated matchups on the Big Ten slate is Penn State and Michigan. It goes way back, and in more seasons than not, there's a lot on the line. This year was no different, except the stakes were simply about preventing their respective seasons from getting any worse. Matt Campbell's Nittany Lions entered with a rough 3-3 record, while Kyle Whittingham and the Wolverines came in at 0-2 in Big Ten play, and looking to avoid dropping to 3-3. BRYCE UNDERWOOD ADDRESSES KYLE WHITTINGHAM'S COMMENTS ABOUT REMAINING STARTING QB AT MICHIGAN Penn State was first to get on the board. The Nittany Lions capped off their opening drive with a 24-yard field goal from kicker Ryan Barker after the Rocco Becht-led offense fizzled out in the red zone. The Nittany Lions absolutely dominated on the time of possession front, staying on offense for nearly two-thirds of the half. But with the Wolverines threatening to tie the game with a field goal of their own or more on a strong late drive, Penn State freshman Josiah Zayas picked off Michigan's Bryce Underwood with an impressive interception. That was Underwood's second interception of the first half, and with offense tough to come by, the Wolverines made a decision to throw freshman Tommy Carr under center to see if he could jump-start the offense. He received a big ovation from fans at the Big House. Unfortunately for the Wolverines, Carr's first drive of the game was a quick three-and-out that was almost entirely on the ground, save for one 3-yard pass. However, they got the ball right back as Becht threw an interception on the first play of the ensuing drive, putting the ball right back in Carr's hands with solid field position just past midfield. That's when Bryson Kuzdzal used his legs to get the Wolverines on the board with an impressive 43-yard run to the end zone. Later in the quarter, Carr took matters into his own hands and rushed the ball up to the Penn State 1-yard line on what was initially ruled a touchdown but was reviewed and marked short. A couple of plays later, running back Jordan Marshall forced his way across the goal line for six. Penn State finally scored a touchdown a few minutes into the fourth quarter to make it a one-possession game, and made it even closer by converting on their two-point attempt to pull within a field goal. However, with five minutes left in regulation and Penn State threatening to score, Becht was hauled down while scrambling and fumbled the ball, which was recovered by Michigan. It was especially costly because it took only a few plays for Carr to score his first career touchdown on a 12-yard run. But it wasn't over just yet. Becht connected with Chase Sowell — who had 11 catches for 151 yards on the day — for a touchdown. OHIO STATE SNAPS INDIANA'S 22-GAME WINNING STREAK, HANDS REIGNING CHAMPS FIRST LOSS SINCE 2024 IN THRILLER However, Penn State's attempt at an onside kick was swallowed up by the Wolverines, and that was it. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A huge win for the Wolverines and a coming-out party for Tommy Carr, who went 5-for-7 passing for 47 yards, all of which came in the second half. On the other side, that's a crushing loss for a Nittany Lions team that certainly didn't need any more games going in the loss column. Michigan will look to keep the momentum going against defending champion Indiana Hoosiers, while Penn State will have a much-needed week off before facing Purdue in Happy Valley on Halloween.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian vows to 'evaluate everything,' won’t rule out benching Arch Manning amid Texas' two-game skid
articles.summary: Arch Manning's late strip-sack fumble sealed Florida's 27-24 upset win over Texas as Steve Sarkisian says he will evaluate "everything," including a potential quarterback change.
articles.body: Florida's 2026 season got off to a strong start, with the Gators moving to 4-0 after upsetting then-No. 4 Ole Miss in Week 4. Florida then dropped their next two games. Despite entering this Saturday's game at Texas on a two-game skid and as an underdog, a late game sack-fumble by Arch Manning sealed a 30-27 upset victory for Florida. Texas has struggled against Florida in recent history, losing to the Gators 29-21 in October 2025. That Florida team went on to finish 4-8. The past eight days have been particularly painful for the Longhorns, who suffered a crushing loss to Oklahoma last week that cost them the No. 1 ranking. Following back-to-back losses to struggling SEC opponents, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said everything was under consideration as he looked to get the team back on track. UNRANKED OKLAHOMA KNOCKS OFF NO. 1 TEXAS IN WALK-OFF FASHION AFTER ARCH MANNING'S ROUGH 4TH QUARTER "Everything’s going to be evaluated," Sarkisian said. He also did not rule out a potential change at quarterback. "Everything means everything," Sarkisian said. "It would be easy for me to say, 'Hey, Arch was the problem today.' Was Arch perfect? No. But nobody was perfect on offense today." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Sarkisian added that the opening quarter was the Longhorns’ lone bright spot. "Obviously, I'm extremely disappointed," he said. "We didn't play very good football today, outside about the first quarter. We kind of bled out." Texas finished Saturday's game with only 50 offensive snaps, the lowest total in Sarkisian’s tenure. Florida sacked Manning five times. Manning's day ended with 173 passing yards and one touchdown pass. Texas entered the day having defeated 22 consecutive unranked opponents at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium. The Longhorns now hold the dubious distinction of being just the third team since 1936 to reach No. 1 in the AP poll before losing consecutive games to unranked opponents, according to ESPN Research. UNRANKED AUBURN UPSETS TOP-RANKED GEORGIA WITH WALK-OFF FIELD GOAL, MARKING WILD FEAT NOT SEEN IN 36 YEARS Sarkisian offered a blunt assessment of how Texas has performed recently. "We're not playing very good football right now," he said. "I have to evaluate everything. It's gonna be a long night." Sarkisian also calls Texas’ offensive plays, meaning his own role will likely be part of the evaluation process. "I don't know how many times I need to say it," Sarkisian said. "We're going to evaluate everything from an offensive perspective. Part of that is playcalling." Texas will host Ole Miss in Austin next Saturday.

articles.title: Panthers Make NHL History as Brady Tkachuk, Carter Verhaeghe Combine for Rare Hat-Trick Stat
articles.summary: The Florida Panthers made history during the team's 8-3 win over the Seattle Kraken on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Florida Panthers made history during the team's 8-3 win over the Seattle Kraken on Saturday.

With Carter Verhaeghe's natural hit trick during the contest, the Panthers became the first team in NHL history to accomplish the feat in three consecutive games (via Jesse Granger of The Athletic).

Brady Tkachuk previously recorded back-to-back natural hat tricks during Florida's wins over the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday and the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday.

Sam Bennett matched Verhaeghe with three goals of his own against Seattle on Saturday, as they became the first Panthers teammates to record hat tricks in the same game.

Florida has opened its 2026-27 campaign on a high note, improving to 5-2-2 with the win over the Kraken.

The Panthers captured the Stanley Cup in both 2024 and 2025, but failed to advance to the playoffs last season.

Tkachuk has been crucial to Florida's early success this year, amassing six goals and four assists in nine contests. Verhaeghe has similarly recorded six goals while picking up two assists.

articles.title: Rays Bounce Back to Beat Guardians 7-3, Even ALCS at Two Games
articles.summary: Tampa Bay’s Offense Comes Alive Late as Yandy Díaz Delivers Insurance Home Run The Tampa Bay Rays responded when they needed it most, defeating the Cleveland...
articles.body:
Tampa Bay's Offense Comes Alive Late as Yandy Díaz Delivers Insurance Home Run

The Tampa Bay Rays responded when they needed it most, defeating the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 on Saturday night to even the American League Championship Series at two games apiece. After falling behind in the series, Tampa Bay delivered a strong offensive performance at Progressive Field, scoring seven runs and taking advantage of Cleveland's defensive mistakes.

The victory puts the Rays back on level terms in the best-of-seven series, with both teams now needing two more wins to advance. Tampa Bay's ability to generate offense in the middle and late innings proved to be the difference in a game that remained competitive for much of the night.

Cleveland opened the scoring in the first inning when Chase DeLauter delivered an RBI single against Tampa Bay starter Nick Martinez. The Rays responded in the third inning, with Jonathan Aranda driving in a run to tie the game at 1-1.

The score remained close until the sixth inning, when Junior Caminero doubled home a run to give Tampa Bay a 2-1 advantage. Caminero's hit provided an important breakthrough for an offense looking to build momentum after struggling to create consistent scoring opportunities earlier in the series.

Tampa Bay continued putting pressure on Cleveland's pitching staff, setting the stage for a decisive seventh inning.

The Rays created separation in the seventh inning, adding three runs to extend their lead to 5-1. Aranda delivered another RBI single, while Chandler Simpson added a sacrifice fly to help Tampa Bay capitalize on its scoring opportunities.

Cleveland attempted to respond in the bottom half of the inning. Travis Bazzana launched a solo home run, and Brayan Rocchio followed with an RBI single to cut the deficit to 5-3.

The Guardians had brought themselves back within striking distance, but Tampa Bay's bullpen limited the damage and prevented Cleveland from completing the comeback.

Yandy Díaz delivered the biggest insurance hit in the ninth inning, launching a two run home run to push Tampa Bay's advantage to 7-3.

The Rays then turned to Bryan Baker, who struck out Angel Martínez to finish the game and secure the important postseason victory.

The win gives Tampa Bay renewed confidence after Cleveland had taken control of the series. The Rays showed they could produce runs against Cleveland's pitching staff while responding to the Guardians' attempts to rally.

With the ALCS now tied 2-2, Sunday's Game 5 becomes a pivotal matchup. Both teams will have an opportunity to move within one victory of reaching the World Series, making the next game especially important.

Tampa Bay needed a response, and the Rays delivered. Their seven run performance evened the series and ensured the ALCS will continue with everything still to play for.

articles.title: Bruins beat the Kings 4-1 for their 5th straight victory
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Marat Khusnutdinov scored in the third period and the Boston Bruins beat the Los Angeles Kings 4-1 on Saturday night for their fifth strai...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Marat Khusnutdinov scored in the third period and the Boston Bruins beat the Los Angeles Kings 4-1 on Saturday night for their fifth straight victory.

David Pastrnak had a goal, Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka scored empty-netters, and Jeremy Swayman made 25 saves. The Bruins swept the three California teams as part of a four-game trip that ends in Dallas on Tuesday.

Alex Laferriere scored for Los Angeles, and Anton Forsberg made 24 saves. The Kings remained winless through six games to start the season and were held to one goal for the fourth straight contest.

Khusnutdinov put the Bruins ahead 2-1 with 6:24 remaining, scoring on a backhander after Forsberg failed to cover up Morgan Geekie's shot and Matt Poitras kept the puck alive.

The Kings got off to a quick start, scoring 31 seconds into the game. Laferriere was at the top of the crease to put in Adrian Kempe's pass for his second goal of the season, making the most of his promotion to first-line center.

But the Bruins responded early in the second period, with Pastrnak tying it at 2:43. He pounced on a loose puck in the neutral zone and took it the other way to beat Forsberg on a wrist shot from the right circle for his fourth goal.

It was Pastrnak's 289th goal at even-strength, tying Phil Esposito for third-most in Boston history.

Bruins center Pavel Zacha did not play because of an upper-body injury he sustained in the third period against the Ducks on Friday. He is day to day, coach Marco Sturm said before the game.

articles.summary: Meadowbrook's Vincent Campbell and John Glenn's Ashlynn Kuklica ruled the roost at the Muskingum Valley League Cross Country meet on Oct. 17.
articles.body:
McLUNEY — It was a two-man fight for supremacy at the Muskingum Valley League Cross Country meet on Oct. 17 at Crooksville High School.

Meadowbrook's Vincent Campbell, a sophomore seeking a second title, and Sheridan's Hudson Wilson had established themselves as favorites based on past performance, a trend that continued with individual league titles on the line.

It was Campbell who won this time, clocking at 16:27 to win the 68-runner Boys Division. His teammate, junior Luke Norman, was third at 17:36.8 as the Colts, who also had senior Grady Forbes (15th, 19:00) and senior Gavin Koscoe (19:24.4) in the top 20, were second with 61 points. Morgan was third with 63.

Wilson (16:39.4) was 12 seconds back but was still runner-up to lead three of coach J.D. Walters' Generals in the top six — freshman Logan Adams (17:50.3) was fifth and Connor Heath sixth (18:01.4). Junior Aiden O'Reilly was 11th (18:50.7) as Sheridan won the team title with 40 points.

Juniors Carson Steimer (7th, 18:11.7), Rylan Tom (9th, 18:32.1), Brandon Haines (10th, 18:46) and sophomore Jordan Blackburn (13th, 18:52.0) paced Morgan; freshman Owen Lahmers was 25th (19:52.6).

Crooksville junior Luke Sheets was fourth in 17:50.2 and Tri-Valley's Alex Hogue was eighth in 18:14.5.

Kuklica wins three-way fight for girls crown

Much like the boys race, the Girls Division was top heavy with three clear favorites in John Glenn senior Ashlynn Kuklica, Tri-Valley senior Erin Hogue and Sheridan senior Sheriden Glanemann.

Kuklica's penchant for rising in big meets continued in Perry County, running a 19:28.0 to win by 20 seconds among 64 runners. Her teammate, sophomore Addy Kent, was ninth (21:53.7).

Hogue, the defending champion, was second (19:48.1) and Glanemann third (19:53.8) — the next-closest finisher was West M senior Ayla Mowery, who clocked in at more than a minute later at 20:59.9 to take fourth.

Sheridan also had junior Adriana Pack (5th, 21:24.1), sophomore Eva Jones (6th, 21:30.3) and senior Addie Dennis (11th, 22:18.1) in the top 15 as it cruised to the team title with 38 points.

Second-place Tri-Valley also saw sophomore Cam Cunningham take 10th (22:15.1), junior Jordyn Frost 16th (23:52.2) and junior Rylee Frost 25th (24:21.7).

Morgan featured three in the top 20 in senior Elana Wilson (7thm 21:40.2), freshman Dakota Johnson (12th, 22:48.4) and freshman Ivy Heagen (19thm 24:03.9).

articles.title: Duke under fire after CB swatted away female athletic trainer tending to Landan Callahan’s injury
articles.summary: Duke Blue Devils CB Kimari Robinson is at the centre of a controversy after aggressively swatting away a female athletic trainer who came onto the field to t...
articles.body:
Duke Blue Devils CB Kimari Robinson is at the centre of a controversy after aggressively swatting away a female athletic trainer who came onto the field to treat teammate Landan Callahan.

The Blue Devils lost a rivalry game against the North Carolina Tar Heels 24-20 and might have lost two key defenders over one incident, although only one of the two got injured.

After CB Landan Callahan went down with an injury, leading to a concerned Kimari Robinson hovering over him, Robinson made a huge mistake by swatting away a female athletic trainer who came to work on Callahan.

Kimari Robinson under extreme scrutiny after swatting away a female athletic trainer

After Callahan went down in the third quarter, Robinson had his moment with trainer Grace Dietrich, prompting a lot of angry fans to criticise his behaviour.

"The kid needs to be benched for a game or two, and forced to go through the emergency training again. You can't have someone that big and strong, acting like that in an emergency. Imagine if he had accidentally connected and floored her, giving her a concussion? Suddenly he'd be up on assault charges, and there would be a second medical emergency distracting the medics trying to help his teammate," said a fan .

"He's a punk, and Duke better make sure he learns a lesson from this," said another angry fan .

"Unacceptable, I have to let the medical staff do what they need to do," said one fan .

"Player should not be there. Let the medical staff do their job. They clearly suspect a neck injury, as the ATC is immobilising the head. She is clearly just trying to make room to do her job," said another fan who was angry at the player .

"I get your point, but the emotions of a kid when someone as close as family is hurting and down isn't a thing to dismiss either. They both obviously care for the down player," said one fan in defence of the player .

With some calling for consequences like missing games for Robinson, the Blue Devils will be left in a tough spot. While they have to discipline the 21-year-old, they also need him on the field after a 1-2 start to the season.

Robinson has five tackles in two games for the Blue Devils as a starting CB, registering three against the Tar Heels.

articles.title: ‘This definitely helped’: Four-star Gaige Weddle on whether BYU could move into his top group
articles.summary: Four-star safety Gaige Weddle was at BYU on Saturday night in its beyond thrilling victory over Notre Dame and now the question will become if the Cougars ca...
articles.body:
Gaige Weddle had nothing to say after his experience at BYU on Saturday night.

He was too shocked, too excited, too enthralled by what he lived through – a life memory – that the four-star safety from Rancho Bernardo , Calif., did not know how to express himself.

"I'm speechless, seriously," Weddle said. "We all are."

BYU took down Notre Dame in Provo on Saturday night, scored the go-ahead touchdown with less than two minutes left and then had something of a long goal-line stand to stifle the Irish in the closing seconds.

ESPN College Gameday was in town. LaVell Edwards Stadium was rocking like maybe never before. After the Cougars held Notre Dame out of the end zone – albeit on a controversial no-call pass interference on the final play – everyone stormed the field in utter jubilation.

Weddle was right there to experience it all.

"What a sick game," Weddle said. "Wow. Wow. Wow."

The question now becomes whether this BYU experience moves the needle enough to get the Cougars into the highest group of programs in his recruitment.

Trips to UCLA (Oct. 24), Oklahoma (Oct. 31), back to Utah (Nov. 7), Georgia (Nov. 14), Miami (Nov. 21) and Ohio State (Nov. 28) are all coming up.

For months, Georgia , Ohio State and Utah have been the three frontrunners with Oklahoma also in that top group. He's a legacy with the Utes since his father, Eric, starred there before playing for more than a decade in the NFL. He'll return to Utah in a few weeks.

This offseason, Weddle had planned to not take as many visits because he had seen many of his favorites last season. But the four-star rethought that decision and this weekend's trip to BYU only solidified his belief that getting back on the road was important.

But can the Cougars crack that top group after his experience Saturday night?

articles.title: Quarterback JP Holsombake throws Mosley past Rickards in district win
articles.summary: Mosley football hadn't played since Sep. 25, so the Dolphins had plenty to prove Saturday night.
articles.body:
PANAMA CITY, Fla. — Mosley continued its dominant run against Leon County competition Saturday night, defeating Rickards 49-14 at Deane Bozeman Field to improve to 7-0 and move within one win of securing the Class 4A District 2 championship.

The Dolphins leaned on a balanced offensive attack led by senior quarterback JP Holsombake, who threw four touchdown passes. Three went to wide receiver Ga'Marcus Halstead, while Khalil Lauderdale hauled in the other. Running back Sammy Chisolm also found the end zone, and sophomore running back Kayden Seay added two rushing touchdowns as Mosley pulled away for another decisive victory.

The win came after a three-week break, but the Dolphins showed little rust as they continued their undefeated season.

Holsombake credited the team's leadership and preparation for its ability to remain focused.

"I'll give it to God first and foremost, but I think leadership played a big role in that," Holsombake said. "We've had three weeks off, and we're playing on a Saturday night, but leadership makes sure the guys are in check and focused on the game."

Holsombake's preparation also paid dividends against the Raiders' defense. The senior quarterback said studying film helped him anticipate what Rickards would do before the play developed.

"I watched a lot of film on my own, so I kind of knew what they were going to do before they did," Holsombake said. "It was just reading the defense and getting the ball to my playmakers."

Mosley's defense continued to reinforce its reputation as one of the team's biggest strengths, limiting Rickards to 14 points while creating opportunities for the Dolphins' offense.

"We felt coming into this year that we had a chance to have the best defense that we've had in my time here at Mosley," said coach Tommy Joe Whiddon said. "I think our defense has proven that over the course of the year."

Whiddon acknowledged that the Dolphins were not flawless, but he was pleased with the overall effort, particularly the defense's ability to create turnovers.

"I thought tonight, at times, our tackling was not great, but I think our energy and effort were good," Whiddon said. "Obviously, Kingston got a pick, and he forced the fumble that Dominick scooped up. So, again, guys making plays."

The game briefly turned tense in the first half when a skirmish broke out along the Mosley sideline. Players from both teams were separated, and the Dolphins went on to maintain control of the contest.

Whiddon said the team would address moments of lost focus while continuing to build toward the postseason.

Mosley closed out another convincing district victory, extending its unbeaten start to 7-0. The Dolphins now turn their attention to their biggest test of the regular season. Mosley will travel to Leon (7-0) on Friday, Oct. 23, with the Class 4A District 2 title on the line.
