articles.title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 Results As Will Ospreay Predictably Wins Clockwork Carnage
articles.summary: Will Ospreay prevailed in an entertaining Clockwork Carnage match that came down to the final seconds at AEW WrestleDream 2026.
articles.body:
Will Ospreay won the inaugural Clockwork Carnage, scoring a pinfall victory over Adam Copeland in the final 10 seconds. Ospreay led the pack with three pinfall victories, while Darby Allin, Adam Copeland and Samoa Joe were locked in a three-way tie with two wins apiece. Kazuchika Okada and Ricochet scored one pinfall each while Speedball Mike Bailey and Konosuke Takeshita were eliminated.

After an emotional victory over Kenny Omega as part of an all-time presentation, at AEW All in 2026 , Will Ospreay embarks in a unique match type at AEW WrestleDream 2026. Ospreay will be defending the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in Clockwork Carnage, a match designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, which frequently collaborates with Will Ospreay.

Between Ospreay being the lowkey brainchild of Clockwork Carnage as well as being early in his world title run, all signs pointed to Ospreay retaining the AEW World Championship at All In.

AEW Clockwork Carnage Rules | AEW WrestleDream 2026

Eight wrestlers compete inside Clockwork Carnage.

Two wrestlers start the match, selected at random.

Every three minutes, another randomly selected wrestler enters.

Until all eight wrestlers have entered, any wrestler who is pinned or submits is eliminated.

Once the final wrestler enters, all remaining wrestlers enter a 15-minute scoring period.

During those 15 minutes, every pinfall or submission scores one fall.

When time expires, the wrestler with the most falls wins.

Will Ospreay Wins Clockwork Carnage | Entrance Order

Konosuke Takeshita | 1 Pinfall (Eliminated by Okada)

Speedball Mike Bailey (Eliminated by Takeshita)

Will Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita started Clockwork Carnage at a faster pace despite having to last for 30 minutes. Takeshita gorilla-pressed Ospreay from the top rope and and blasted Ospreay with a flying clothesline. The pace quickened, and Takeshita hit a dive to the outside on Ospreay.

Bailey wore United Empire colors, but Excalibur reminded viewers that there are no friends in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita wiped out Bailey and went back to work on Ospreay to the delight of the crowd. Ospreay and Speedball showed solidarity with a United Empire high-five. Takeshita broke it up immediately and fans supported it.

Ricochet tried to bargain with Takeshita so they could work together against the UE. The strategy worked temporarily until Twitter Ricky tried to roll up Takeshita for a nearfall. Ricochet rebounded with a dive to Ospreay on the outside. Ricochet tried a chop on Takeshita to no avail. His forearms didn't work either. One headbutt from Takeshita dropped Ricochet like a WWE roster cut.

Ospreay and Bailey hit a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay tried to vulture the pin and failed. Darby Allin flew in with a skateboard and hit an ollie on Ricochet's back. Darby set up a table outside of the ring.

Ospreay looked nearly defeated when Kazuchika Okada's music hit after three more minutes of Clockwork Carnage. Okada hit a textbook dropkick on Darby Allin, sending him crashing to the mat.

Takeshita eliminated Bailey with a Burning Hammer. Adam Copeland was out next and fans popped huge. Fans sang Cope's music as he set up Ricochet for a spear. Cope missed the spear and landed face-first into the turnbuckle. Copeland blocked Ricochet's moonsault with his knees.

Okada came flying in and hit a Rainmaker on Takeshita for the elimination. Samoa Joe ran down as the final entrant. Ricochet went for a tope, and Joe said "Nope."

The 15-minute interval came down to a Final 6 with Takeshita and Mike Bailey eliminated. What followed was a parade of pinfalls with everybody scoring one pin except Copeland. Darby took the lead with a pin on Cope.

Cope speared Ricochet out of the ring and through the table. A great spot, but as Tony Schiavone noted, you've got to pin people to win Clockwork Carnage. With less than six minutes remaining in Clockwork Carnage, Ospreay and Allin were deadlocked at two pins apiece. Everybody else had one pin with the exception of Cope who was stuck at zero.

Samoa Joe dodged two separate Oscutters with the Nope spot. Joe pounced on Ospreay with a Coquina Clutch. Nigel McGuinness wisely advised Ospreay to tap with time running out in Clockwork Carnage. Ospreay finally tapped, giving Joe two wins. At the three-minute mark, there was a three-way tie between Ospreay, Allin and Joe.

Copeland got on the board late with a pair of spears on Samoa Joe and Ricochet at the two-minute mark. Now it was a four-way tie. In a wild final 90 seconds filled with nearfalls, Ospreay stumbled his way to a Hidden Blade attempt, but Cope dodged it and hit an Impaler on Ospreay. 60 seconds left.

Cope went for a spear, but Okada cut him off. Copeland hit a spear on Okada and pinned Okada with 10 seconds left. Ospreay cut him off with a Hidden Blade at the buzzer for the win. Fans seemed disappointed this match didn't go to overtime, but it was fun while it lasted.

articles.title: Sebastian Fundora Scored Buzzer-Beater TKO — But Terence Crawford Says It Shouldn’t Have Counted
articles.summary: Sebastian Fundora vs. Ermal Hadribeaj results: a 12th-round TKO kept Fundora’s WBC title, but Terence Crawford and Tim Bradley criticized referee Thomas Tayl...
articles.body:
Sebastian Fundora is incapable of delivering a boring fight. The WBC super welterweight champion successfully defended his title with a 12th-round TKO over Ermal Hadribeaj. The fight wasn't just a KO in the final round, it was a buzzer-beating shot that appeared to land after the bell. Hadribeaj was hurt and reeling from Fundora's last-ditch effort to get the stoppage when he went down from a long, straight left hand.

Hadribeaj got to his feet before referee Thomas Taylor's 10 count. However, despite the fight being over, Taylor assessed Hadribeaj and waved off the rest of the count, scoring it a TKO win for Fundora. The reaction to the finish was as spirited as you might expect.

The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan, Las Vegas

Fundora def. Hadribeaj, TKO, Round 12 (2:59)

Hadribeaj, Rounds 3 and 11 (holding in Round 3)

Did Thomas Taylor Get the Fundora-Hadribeaj Finish Wrong?

During the post-fight breakdown, Terence Crawford and Timothy Bradley made it known they believed Taylor acted incorrectly in that situation. Bradley said, "I love Thomas Taylor. He's one of the best in the business. But just like fighters can have an off night, referees can too and he had an off night tonight."

Crawford said, "What else was he supposed to do? He got to his feet. He deserved to go the distance."

How Did Sebastian Fundora Look Against Ermal Hadribeaj?

Aside from that finish, Fundora was well in control of the fight and set to win a clear decision without the KO. While he was in line for a win, many pointed out his flawed performance. Hadribeaj had some success in the early rounds, landing looping power shots on the inside.

Hadribeaj entered the fight unbeaten at 23-0-1 as Fundora's mandatory challenger. Taylor deducted a point from him for holding in the third round and took another in the 11th.

To Fundora's credit, the punches didn't appear to have much effect. However, with a potential unification fight on the horizon against Jaron "Boots" Ennis (should he beat Josh Kelly), many believe Fundora was exposed on Saturday night. Crawford took to X during the fight and kept it simple and plain as he looked ahead to that fight.

Fundora's height, stamina and heart make him one of the most exciting fighters in the world. Fight fans have their fingers crossed for a unification fight between him and Boots.

articles.title: College football faces another clock controversy after BYU upsets Notre Dame
articles.summary: BYU's Bear Bachmeier scored three touchdowns as the unbeaten Cougars stunned Notre Dame 28-24, snapping the Fighting Irish's 16-game winning streak.
articles.body: It was a wild Saturday in college football, and if top team after top team taking losses wasn’t crazy enough, another game ended with a one-second clock controversy. BYU pulled off an upset over Notre Dame — but social media seems to think the game may not have actually been over. Thanks to the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs losing at home to Auburn, No. 2 Notre Dame had a chance to take over the top spot with a win. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Unfortunately, they would have to do that on the road against the Big 12's top team, the unbeaten No. 8 BYU Cougars. And, to make matters worse, the Fighting Irish were without one of their best defensive players almost immediately. On BYU's first series, defensive lineman Boubacar Traore was called for targeting on a hit on BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. That was a costly penalty for a team that doesn't take a lot of them, and the Cougars made them pay. They marched downfield — even forcing Notre Dame to burn a timeout — with Bachmeier finding the end zone to open the scoring. Notre Dame hit a field goal in the first quarter and then found the end zone in the second with running back Nolan James Jr. hitting paydirt to give them a 10-7 lead. However, BYU had more, particularly a trick play that saw Bachmeier trotting into the end zone with the help of a blocker. Then, as if that wasn't enough, Bachmeier scored another touchdown using his legs just before the half, and with the extra point, that gave BYU a 21-10 lead. However, there was still enough time for Notre Dame to get another possession, and with just nine seconds on the clock, the Fighting Irish found themselves on the BYU 5-yard line. Notre Dame QB CJ Carr attempted to spike the ball, but he never had total control of it, and upon review, it was ruled a fumble, with the Irish leaving points on the table and forking over possession. Notre Dame battled back in the second half, and eventually found themselves up by a field goal. BYU responded when Bachmeier — who had already shown he can find the end zone as a rusher and receiver — threw his first passing touchdown of the game by finding tight end Walker Lyons with just under two minutes left in regulation. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! That gave BYU a four-point lead and meant Notre Dame couldn't settle for a field goal. The Irish converted on a crucial fourth-and-2 to keep their drive alive, but after failing to get into the end zone, they found themselves facing fourth-and-five with ten seconds remaining. They managed to convert with four seconds on the clock, setting up the final play of the game. There was some contact on that one, but no flags. That'll frustrate Notre Dame fans, but not as much as this will. Uh... not that again. The field had been stormed, and both teams had headed to the locker room before that started making the rounds on social media. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Nonetheless, what a game. That ended Notre Dame's 16-game winning streak and is one of several outcomes that are going to shake up the rankings and CFP picture in a big, big way. Notre Dame will take a week off and then get back at it against Navy, while the Cougars will keep chugging along with a visit to Orlando to take on the UCF Knights.

articles.title: Unlikely 16-year streak continues after Alabama lose to Tennessee
articles.summary: Alabama football’s struggles continued on Saturday as the Tennessee Volunteers handed the Crimson Tide a disappointing 26-10 loss at Neyland Stadium. Kalen D...
articles.body:
Alabama football 's struggles continued on Saturday as the Tennessee Volunteers handed the Crimson Tide a disappointing 26-10 loss at Neyland Stadium. Kalen DeBoer's team suffered another setback in Knoxville, with the loss extending an unwanted streak that dates back 16 years.

The Volunteers secured their third consecutive home victory over Alabama in the rivalry. A notable 16-year statistic emerged following the loss, as the last time Alabama lost an away game without fans storming the field was in 2010 against LSU.

Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell endured a challenging afternoon against Tennessee's defense. He completed 19 of his 29 pass attempts for 147 yards but threw two interceptions.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Alabama's turnover problems proved equally damaging, as the Crimson Tide surrendered possession twice on fumbles in addition to Russell's interceptions. Tennessee took advantage of those costly mistakes, using the extra opportunities and favorable field position to maintain control of the game.

DeBoer was candid when discussing his team's offensive struggles during the postgame press conference.

"Just struggled to sustain anything," DeBoer said. Keeping drives and continuity there. A penalty or came up short on a couple of fourth downs. You're going to have to find a way to get some explosives against a front like that. We struggled to do that. Turnovers early, gave them some field position. They got the points."

The defeat leaves Tennessee with a 6-1 overall record and a 3-1 mark in SEC play, while Alabama falls to 5-2 overall and 3-2 in conference competition. The result also marks Alabama's first consecutive regular-season losses since 2007 after their recent loss against Georgia .

Alabama will return to Tuscaloosa next week for its Homecoming matchup against Texas A&M. The Crimson Tide will look to bounce back in front of their home fans and prevent their losing streak from extending to three consecutive games.

articles.title: Kirby Smart explains why Gunner Stockton left the Auburn game
articles.summary: “I don't think so," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said on if Gunner Stockton's injury impacted his performance vs. Auburn. "He's had that before.”
articles.body:
ATHENS, Ga. - Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton went down after taking a hit on a designed carry on the first play of Georgia's 27-24 loss to the Auburn Tigers . Stockton left for several plays before returning to action. Stockton was forced to be checked for a concussion by the medical staff.

Following Georgia's loss, coach Kirby Smart provided an injury update on Stockton.

"Well, they (Georgia's training staff) checked him out and said he was good," Smart said. "He had a stinger in his shoulder, which, you know, numbs your shoulder, but that happens a lot in football and you come back from that. But they were checking him for you know, concussion and things. They checked him out and brought him back in and said he was cleared."

Stockton had his worst performance of the season against Auburn . He threw a pair of interceptions and had a critical fumble late in Georgia's loss, which set up Auburn's game-winning drive when Georgia was hoping to go on its own game-winning drive.

"I don't think so," Smart said on if Stockton's injury impacted his performance. "He's had that before."

Stockton finished the Auburn game completing 22 of 34 passes for 272 passing yards. He threw two touchdowns and two interceptions. He ran the ball nine times for 26 yards. To Stockton's credit, he led Georgia on a 94-yard touchdown drive to tie the game with under three minutes left in the fourth quarter.

Fortunately for Georgia, the Bulldogs have a bye week to regroup after a tough loss. It is clear that Stockton is going to have to play better if Georgia is going to have a successful season.

articles.title: 3 quick takeaways from Badgers loss to UCLA: Wisconsin gets outcoached in disappointing outing
articles.summary: The Badgers squandered a huge opportunity on the road on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Wisconsin Badgers dropped their second game of the season in a 17-7 loss to the No. 12 UCLA Bruins on Saturday, as they fell to 4-2 and 2-1 in conference play.

It was a very disappointing outing for the Badgers, who had plenty of opportunities on both sides of the ball, but could not score points or get off the field on third downs.

As a result, they squandered a potential chance to be in the AP Top 25 next week, and now are set to face a tough two-week slate with the No. 19 USC Trojans and the No. 17 Iowa Hawkeyes up next in season-defining games.

Here are three quick takeaways from the Badgers 17-7 loss to UCLA.

There were moments in this game where I thought both coaches made questionable decisions, with UCLA's trick-play interception standing out for the Bruins. But, far more often than not, in a game that was there for the taking, Luke Fickell was outcoached by Bob Chesney, making a couple of headscratching field position decisions.

The first major one came on Wisconsin's second offensive drive, as the Badgers got to a 4th & 2 at the 50-yard line following UCLA's 16-play, 84-yard field goal drive that lasted 8:42. After a bevy of questionable penalties, the Badgers, who had initially gotten to the UCLA 43-yard line, got back to the 50-yard line for a 4th & 2 after a 23-yard catch from Jaylon Domingeaux.

Wisconsin had just seen UCLA march down the field with a long, sustained drive on its defense. Regardless, though, of their confidence in the defense, it felt like a clear go-for situation, with the chance to respond and put points on the board, or at least give their offense more plays.

Instead, the Badgers punted, and their defense allowed a 13-play, 91-yard touchdown drive, negating the field advantage.

That wasn't the only time Wisconsin punted in neutral or plus territory. The Badgers had a huge opportunity, facing a 1st & 10 at the UCLA 39-yard line in a 10-7 game in the third quarter after a 15-yard completion on first down and a UCLA penalty. Wisconsin had just scored a touchdown on a drive that consisted of 10 rushing plays and one pass.

In a favorable situation, Jeff Grimes didn't extend off his creativity from the previous drive in the run game, where Wisconsin was clearly clicking. Instead, Wisconsin threw an incompletion on first down, got nothing on a Colton Joseph-designed run up the middle, and had an incompletion on third down where Joseph missed an open Chris Brooks after extending the play.

There were a few questionable decisions on the drive. First was the choice not to continue riding the ground game with the different looks they threw at UCLA. At the very least, Wisconsin needed to get six yards to get into field goal range or get a potential go-for situation on second and third down. Instead, the Badgers punted in plus territory down three.

And just like the previous two times, the Bruins made Wisconsin pay, going 89 yards on six plays for their second touchdown of the game.

But the waving of the white flag came with five minutes left and the Badgers down 10 points after the defense forced a three-and-out. Once again, Wisconsin couldn't get anything on their first three downs and faced a 4th & 9 with 4:54 left down two scores. Here, Luke Fickell elected to punt, and the Badgers never got the ball back.

After the game, Fickell said he wanted the offense to get into a better situation with six or seven yards to go, but Wisconsin was very likely not getting the ball back twice, let alone once, which is what happened on Saturday. Instead, the Badgers ended the game with their defense on the field as UCLA converted a pair of key third downs and drove down the field again.

Third downs cost Wisconsin the game on both sides of the ball.

Wisconsin's defense, which had been elite at getting off the field on third downs, just could not do so on Saturday. UCLA was 13 of 20 on third downs. And it wasn't like the Bruins were really getting explosives. Instead, they slowly churned down the field on a number of drives, going 16, 13, 7, 12, 6, and 9 plays on six of their nine drives.

They dominated time of possession as a result (37:02 to 22:58), and they especially converted well on their long scoring drives. On their first drive, UCLA converted their first five third downs before failing on the sixth, leading to a field goal in a goal-to-go situation.

On their second drive, they went 4 for 4 on third downs. Wisconsin bailed out the Bruins with some penalties, but the Badgers defense could not get off the field, despite stopping the run at a very high level and forcing the Bruins to have an average of 6.1 yards to go on third downs.

Wisconsin's offense on third downs was a worse story. The Badgers were just 3 of 11 on third downs, but the biggest issue was the average distance to go: 9.4 yards. Penalties absolutely killed Wisconsin in this one, and the Badgers constantly found themselves behind the chains on drives where they finally started to have some momentum.

It's near impossible to win when you have to go 9.4 yards on third downs, especially when Wisconsin's passing offense struggled as much as it did on Saturday, leading to our third takeaway…

In every game this season, win or loss, the Badgers have failed to be consistent for four quarters in the passing game. They've had their moments and hit on some explosive plays, but it's been more struggles than successes so far.

On Saturday, they couldn't find any consistency. Colton Joseph completed just 6 of 16 passes for 66 yards, marking the lowest output of a start in his career. Wisconsin had Jaylon Domingeaux back, but it didn't mean much, as the Badgers got virtually nothing in the air.

Wisconsin even had solid protection at times, although UCLA made sure to send extra to force Joseph into poor decisions. The Badgers struggled on the simple concepts, be it inaccurate throws or a dropped pass on a swing pass. And Joseph's uneven play continued.

The quarterback tried to give some of his receivers some opportunities, but he made a couple of questionable decisions once again. Joseph also held the ball too long at times, which has been a common theme this season.

Joseph's legs are the best part of the offense currently, as it opens up the team's run game to be creative and present different looks as it did for one drive on Saturday. But his struggles in the pass game are well-documented, and UCLA did not give any respect to the aerial attack, loading the box and teeing off with extra rushers.

His receivers did not help either. The biggest question in the offseason was whether Wisconsin's strategy of quantity over getting a clear No. 1 wideout was the right one. Wisconsin's wideouts have had some quality games this season, but separation, specifically against man coverage, has been an issue.

It was never more prevalent than on Saturday against UCLA's sticky defense. The Badgers wideouts could not generate separation and get open, and the connection on 50/50 balls was not there at all. Joseph did have a nice dime to Malachi Coleman in the end zone near the end of the first half on a should-be touchdown.

But Coleman dropped the diving catch, and Wisconsin ended the drive with points after Joseph took a sack on third down and Gavin Lahm missed a 45-yard field goal. Wisconsin had a ton of opportunities on Saturday. Each of their drives, aside from their final one, got to at least their own 40-yard line, with many getting into UCLA territory.

Ending with seven points after that is a disappointment.

articles.title: Alex Tuch has 2 goals and an assist in the Capitals' win over the Canadiens
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Ryan Leonard scored a highlight-reel goal and the Washington Capitals beat the New Jersey Devils 4-2 on Saturday afternoon.Ilya Protas, Dyl...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Ryan Leonard scored a highlight-reel goal and the Washington Capitals beat the New Jersey Devils 4-2 on Saturday afternoon.

Ilya Protas, Dylan Strome and Boone Jenner also scored and Vincent Desharnais had two assists for the Capitals, who have won back-to-back games.

Arsenal Gritsyuk and Timo Meier scored for the Devils, who dropped to 4-4-0 to open the season.

The Devils got on the board first roughly halfway through the first period, when Gritsyuk beat Logan Thompson through traffic at the end of New Jersey's second power play of the period.

With 3:18 to go in the first, though, Leonard would even the score and change the momentum with his spectacular goal. In the final seconds of Washington's power play, Leonard took the puck up ice himself, going coast to coast before beating Luke Hughes, cutting to the inside and deking out Jake Allen for his third goal of the season.

From there, the Capitals took over the game, starting with back-to-back goals in a span of 4 minutes, 46 seconds to open the second period. First, Protas buried a cross-zone feed from Alex Ovechkin to give Washington the 2-1 lead. Then, Strome finished off a passing play from Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou to put Washington up by two.

WINNIPEG, Manitoba (AP) — Nikolaj Ehlers scored a power-play goal 6:43 into the third period to lift Carolina to their seventh straight victory, over Winnipeg.

The former Jet fired a wrist shot past the glove of Clay Stevenson.

Mark Jankowski — also on the power play — and Jesperi Kotkaniemi scored for Carolina as well. Hurricanes defenseman Shayne Gostisbehere had two assists.

Pyotr Kochetkov made 21 saves and has posted victories in all five starts this season. With fewer than 40 seconds remaining, Kochetkov made a pad save on Cole Perfetti, following that up with a save on 18-year-old Viggo Bjorck off the helmet to preserve Carolina's lead.

Mark Scheifele and Alex Iafallo scored for Winnipeg, which lost its first game this season on home ice in regulation. Stevenson stopped 34 shots.

TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — Nikita Kucherov scored twice, Jake Guentzel had a goal and an assist, and Dennis Hildeby stopped 12 shots as Tampa Bay defeated Vancouver.

Guentzel scored the winner in the third period as Tampa Bay came back from a two-goal deficit.

Pontus Holmberg also scored and Brayden Point finished with two assists for Tampa Bay, which improved to 5-0 at home.

Linus Karlsson and Elias Pettersson scored while Kevin Lankinen finished with 31 saves for the Canucks, who finished winless (0-4-1) on a five-game road trip. Vancouver is winless in the past seven games (0-6-1) overall.

Guentzel picked up the winner at 2:04 of the third after Charle-Edouard D'Astous slid a pass off the wall to Guentzel for the quick snap shot that deflected off the stick of Vancouver's Liam Ohgren.

For the second consecutive game, the Canucks had a 2-0 lead they were not able to hold.

SUNRISE, Fla. (AP) — Carter Verhaeghe had a history-making natural hat trick, Sam Bennett scored his first three goals of the season and Florida rolled past Seattle

The Panthers became the first team in NHL history with natural hat tricks in three consecutive games, after Brady Tkachuk had them in wins over Columbus on Tuesday and Vancouver on Thursday. Florida also became only the third team in 30 years to have a hat trick — of any variety — in three consecutive games.

With four hat tricks already this season — all coming in the last three games — Florida has matched its total from the last three regular seasons combined. Niko Mikkola and Sam Reinhart also scored for the Panthers, and Matthew Tkachuk had three assists.

Freddy Gaudreau, Shane Wright and Ryker Evans had goals for Seattle, while Kaapo Kakko and Berkly Catton both had two-assist games.

TORONTO (AP) — Bo Horvat scored the winner and added an assist to help the New York beat Toronto.

Simon Holmstrom scored twice, the second into an empty net, and Anthony Duclair also connected for New York (4-3-1). Ilya Sorokin made 28 saves.

Colton Sissons replied for Toronto (3-4-2). Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 16 shots for the Maple Leafs. They have dropped three straight games and four of their last five.

The Islanders jumped out to a 1-0 lead at 8:18 of the first period when Duclair took a pass in the slot and changed the angle before firing through a partial screen on Bobrovsky.

Coming off a hat trick Thursday night in a 5-4 home shootout loss to Buffalo, Maple Leafs winger Kirill Marchenko had a couple of chances that Sorokin turned aside in the second.

No. 1 overall pick Gavin McKenna, who was benched for the second half of Thursday's contest, had an opportunity it late in the second period on a partial breakaway, but fired high and wide. The Islanders raced the other way, with Horvat eventually beating Bobrovsky with 1:27 to go.

MONTREAL (AP) — Cole Caufield scored his second goal of the game 54 seconds into overtime to lift Montreal over Buffalo.

Caufield had a breakaway after Josh Norris missed his shot on a 3-on-1 rush. He ripped a shot into the top-left corner, extending his franchise record with his 14th regular-season overtime goal.

Zachary Bolduc and Alexandre Texier also scored while Montreal built a two-goal lead before Buffalo stormed back. Juraj Slafkovsky and Alexandre Carrier added two assists each.

Jacob Fowler stopped 23 shots in his fourth start in five games.

DETROIT (AP) — Lucas Raymond scored the only goal during the shootout and Detroit rallied for a victory over San Jose.

Alex DeBrincat scored with 1:33 remaining to send the game into overtime. DeBrincat's team-high fifth goal left him one shy of 300 for his career.

Justin Faulk and Emmitt Finnie also scored for the Red Wings, who have won back-to-back wins for the first time this season. John Gibson stopped 32 shots.

Macklin Celebrini had a goal and two assists to lead the Sharks. Dmitry Orlov and Ivar Stenberg contributed power-play goals, while Alex Nedeljkovic made 25 saves in the second of six consecutive road games for San Jose.

With Gibson pulled for an extra skater, DeBrincat tapped in the puck with 1:33 remaining during a scramble in front of the net. Detroit needed to kill off Andrew Copp's penalty in overtime to force the shootout.

PHILEDELPHIA (AP) — Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone each had a goal and an assist, and Philadelphia beat Ottawa for their first victory this season.

Philadelphia (1-6-3) opened with nine consecutive losses, a franchise record.

Michkov set up Martone with a nifty pass to the far post, and Martone tapped in his second goal this season at 9:03 of the second period to tie the score 1-all.

Martone returned the favor on a power play late in the period, firing a shot toward the net that Ottawa goalie Linus Ullmark stopped. But the rebound went right to Michkov, who snapped home his fourth goal of the season at 18:33.

It was the 50th career goal for Michkov in 171 games. He became the fastest Flyers player to reach the milestone since Matt Read in 2014.

Trevor Zegras added an empty-net goal with 14 seconds left in the third to seal it.

COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — Kent Johnson scored with 1:33 remaining on the clock in overtime, Jet Greaves got his fifth career shutout and Columbus beat New York.

Charlie Coyle brought the puck into the zone and passed to Zach Werenski near the left faceoff circle. Werenski then found Johnson in the slot, who fired a wrist shot past Rangers goaltender Dylan Garand for his team-leading fourth goal of the season as the Blue Jackets snapped a two-game slide.

It was Werenski's 22nd career point in overtime. With seven goals and 15 assists, he passed Seth Jones for most overtime points in franchise history.

It was the fourth time the Blue Jackets won 1-0 in overtime. The previous occasion was Feb. 4, 2020, against the Florida Panthers.

CHICAGO (AP) — Jake Oettinger made 19 saves for his NHL-leading third shutout in six games, Arttu Hyry scored twice and Dallas beat Chicago.

Jason Robertson scored and Roope Hintz also connected before he exited late in the third period with a right hand injury. Dallas (4-3-1) won its second straight to give Glen Gulutzan his 200th NHL coaching victory.

Oettinger had his 19th career shutout and lowered his goals-against average to 1.00. The 25-year-old Hyry had his first multi-goal game.

The Stars, who trimmed their NHL-best team goals average to 1.50, outshot the Blackhawks 32-19 in this one and limited Chicago's chances.

Spencer Knight blocked 28 shots in his fourth straight start as the Blackhawks' two-game winning streak ended.

NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Filip Forsberg scored a goal and added an assist to lead Nashville to a victory over St. Louis.

Jonathan Marchessault, Adam Edstrom, Ryan O'Reilly and Jack Drury also scored and Juuse Saros made 24 saves to help the Predators snap a three-game losing streak.

Phillip Broberg and Jimmy Snuggerud scored and Jordan Binnington made 19 saves for the Blues. They have lost consecutive games.

Broberg scored the game's first goal at 6:21 of the opening period. Coming through the slot unchecked, Broberg beat Saros with a wrist shot on the glove side.Mason McTavish assisted on the goal, extending his points streak to six games. He has four goals and four assists over that span.

LOS ANGELES (AP) — Marat Khusnutdinov scored in the third period and Boston beat Los Angeles Kings for their fifth straight victory.

David Pastrnak had a goal, Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka scored empty-netters, and Jeremy Swayman made 25 saves. The Bruins swept the three California teams as part of a four-game trip that ends in Dallas on Tuesday.

Alex Laferriere scored for Los Angeles, and Anton Forsberg made 24 saves. The Kings remained winless through six games to start the season and were held to one goal for the fourth straight contest.

Khusnutdinov put the Bruins ahead 2-1 with 6:24 remaining, scoring on a backhander after Forsberg failed to cover up Morgan Geekie's shot and Matt Poitras kept the puck alive.

The Kings got off to a quick start, scoring 31 seconds into the game. Laferriere was at the top of the crease to put in Adrian Kempe's pass for his second goal of the season, making the most of his promotion to first-line center.

articles.title: Fresno City College Rams stun Modesto in late stages to top league standings
articles.summary: A late-game charge led by Fresno City's special teams and defense proved to be the difference in a thrilling 24-17 win over Modesto.
articles.body:
A late-game charge led by Fresno City's special teams and defense proved to be the difference in a thrilling 24-17 win over Modesto to vault to the top spot in the league standings on Saturday afternoon.

The Rams entered the fourth quarter trailing 17-14, but a forced fumble by Aiden Chavez recovered by Geremy Molett put the Rams in prime position and Jared Roberts delivered, tying the game with an ice-cold field goal.

Fresno City got a stop on the ensuing drive to get the ball back but was forced to punt on their next offensive possession.

Although, being forced to punt proved to be exactly what FCC needed.

Roberts delivered again, this time pinning the Pirates at their own one-yard line, and the defense responded accordingly.

On the next play, the Rams popped the ball free, and Tana Togafau-Tavui fell on the loose ball for the easiest touchdown he'll ever score, and probably the most important.

The Rams took the lead and despite the Pirates driving right down the field, a batted ball with triple zeroes on the clock sealed a crucial win in league play for FCC.

Fresno City now sits tied atop the league standings with Modesto at 5-1 and improves to 8-5 on the season.

articles.title: Hurricanes at Flames: Preview, How to Watch, Game Thread

articles.body:
Hope you enjoyed your three day break as the Hurricanes are right back in action tonight.

The Canes head further west into Canada as they play the first half of the Alberta Duo with the Calgary Flames. Unlike most times when the Canes are against one of the Alberta teams, their next game isn't against the other. In a weird quirk, the Canes will head out even further west to Vancouver on Tuesday before coming back to Alberta on Thursday to play Edmonton before ending the State Fair Road trip against the Blues next week.

On the surface, you'd be excused for having confidence on going into Calgary tonight. Even in a division that many consider the weakest in the NHL they have just one win on the young season—a 4-2 win over Anaheim just this past Tuesday. Every other game has been just a demolition, including their recent 6-2 loss to Vegas on Thursday. Tonight though begins a four-game home stretch in the iconic Saddledome, the last visit the Hurricanes will make to the arena that opened up in the early 80's. Next season, Calgary is set to go to a nice and shiny new arena with all the bells and whistles, but this year has quickly become about celebrating the place they have called home for over 40 years.

With that, expect some sort of feature about how people have to walk a catwalk over the ice in order to get to the press box, and some sort of expression of how happy they are they won't have to do it again.

When you try to look at the stats to find a bright spot on offense for Calgary so far you just can't. There aren't any players with a positive +/-, their leading goal scorers have all of two on the season, the most points anyone has is four, and both goalies have save percentages well under .850 with GAA's that are above four. It's just beyond clear that they are looking to reset as half the current roster is under 26, and the allure of a farewell for the old building plus the shiny new building should be enough to satiate fans while they try to recover.

If there's something that Calgary has in their favor it's the back-to-back versus rest factor. The Flames haven't played since Thursday while the Canes traveled for the second afternoon in a row. They're also still working in two prospects while at least two regulars remain out in Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal. It's also very unlikely that Seth Jarvis will join the team tonight on the ice as they won't have any sort of morning skate today.

That lack of morning skate plus the success of the team against a surprisingly good Winnipeg team means you shouldn't expect any line changes from Rod Brind'Amour. Honestly, there shouldn't be. Jackson Blake and Logan Stankoven functioned just fine with Bradly Naddeau on the other side, and the line centered by Jesperi Kotkaniemi with Eric Robinson and Felix Unger-Sorum helped get Kotkaniemi his first goal in a year. The one change you should see is between the pipes as Brandon Bussi will get his first action in a week. It's not because of his performance against Chicago, it's simply been that Pyotr Kochetkov has played well enough with enough space in between games to earn three starts in a row.

We'll see how Bussi looks after the time off, as this way the schedule falls this week expect to see more of a rotation over the next four games. It does go a long way to quieting the murmuring about the Canes trying to acquire Connor Hellebuyck, whose suspension is set to end for Winnipeg on Friday . The Jets weren't happy with offeres up until now, and it's pretty unlikely the Canes will change it considering how the tandem has done so far. We'll see if Bussi can continue the good play.
